title: Mixed-workload scheduler — benchmark results (baseline vs flag) [sheet]
content:
Doc: Mixed-workload benchmark results sheet (text export)
Owner: Rina Kobayashi
Last updated: 2025-02-11

Notes / how to read
- Baseline = FIFO scheduler (current default), runtime-1.19.0-rc2
- Prototype = mixed-workload scheduler flag ON: scheduler.mixed_workload_v1=true (two-queue + fairness window + starvation guardrails)
- All results are steady-state after warmup. Unless stated, batcher/caching settings unchanged.
- Metrics reported per request end-to-end latency (enqueue -> last token). For streaming, this is time-to-last-token; TTFT is also captured.
- “Short” class ≈ interactive/chat-ish; “Long” class ≈ prefill-heavy (long context / summarization). Classification per PR_8427 + PR_8480 (EWMA refinement) unless scenario forces lengths.
- Units:
  - Latency: ms
  - Throughput: output tokens/sec per GPU (otps/GPU) unless specified
  - GPU util: average SM util % as reported by DCGM
  - Queue depth: mean+max over run
  - Wait time = time in scheduler queue (enqueue -> dispatch)

Config snapshot
- Model: rwi/llama-70b-instruct (internal serving build), fp16 kernels; kv-cache on
- Max batch tokens: 8192 (unchanged)
- Prefill/decode overlap: enabled
- Request limits: default per test; overload scenarios explicitly labeled
- Prototype knobs used for these runs:
  - short_weight=0.85 (share of dispatch opportunities)
  - fairness_window_ms=250
  - max_long_wait_ms=1500 (guardrail)
  - admission_control: separate per-class thresholds ON (PR_8462)

Hardware matrix
- SKU-A: A100 80GB (PCIe) — driver 550.xx, CUDA 12.4, 1xGPU
- SKU-H: H100 80GB (SXM) — driver 550.xx, CUDA 12.4, 1xGPU
- SKU-L: L40S 48GB — driver 550.xx, CUDA 12.4, 1xGPU

============================================================
TAB: Summary (headline deltas)
============================================================
Goal: reduce tail latency for short traffic in mixed workloads without >5% throughput regression; ensure long traffic not starved.

Table: Aggregate delta across mixed scenarios (Short-class p95; Long-class p95; total throughput)

| Hardware | #scenarios | Short p95 median delta | Short p99 median delta | Long p95 median delta | Total throughput median delta |
|---------|------------|------------------------|------------------------|-----------------------|------------------------------|
| SKU-A   | 8          | -29%                   | -24%                   | +6%                   | -1.8%                        |
| SKU-H   | 6          | -23%                   | -18%                   | +4%                   | -1.2%                        |
| SKU-L   | 6          | -19%                   | -16%                   | +8%                   | -2.7%                        |

Starvation checks (all mixed scenarios)
- Long max wait time observed (p100):
  - SKU-A: 1180ms (guardrail 1500ms)
  - SKU-H: 960ms
  - SKU-L: 1410ms (closest to guardrail; see Scenario L-06 notes)
- No “infinite backlog” growth observed when admission_control split enabled. One oscillation case fixed by PR_8468 regression.

============================================================
TAB: Scenario definitions (quick)
============================================================
Scenario IDs used below
- MX-01: 70/30 short/long mix, Poisson arrivals, short prompt 128 toks / gen 128 toks; long prompt 4096 toks / gen 256 toks
- MX-02: 90/10 mix (chat heavy)
- MX-03: 50/50 mix (worst contention)
- MX-04: Burst: 20s at 3x RPS then 40s normal; 80/20 mix
- MX-05: “Long batch window”: long requests arrive in synchronized clumps (every 5s), short steady
- MX-06: Streaming short vs non-streaming long
- TR-01: Trace replay (customer-like) “Support-2194 anonymized” (mixed summarization + chat)
- TR-02: Trace replay “Dedicated noisy-neighbor report” (more long contexts)

============================================================
TAB: Regression gates / pass-fail (draft)
============================================================
Proposed CI/perf gate thresholds for “mixed-workload suite” (aligning with perf standards draft):
- Primary: Short-class p95 must improve by >= 15% in MX-01 and MX-05 on SKU-A
- Secondary: Total throughput regression must be <= 5% in all mixed scenarios (A100/H100/L40S)
- Fairness: Long max wait p100 <= 1500ms (configurable, but must remain <= 2000ms even if tuned)
- Stability: No monotonic growth in long queue depth under steady offered load (slope approx 0 over 10min)

Current status vs draft gates
- SKU-A: PASS
- SKU-H: PASS
- SKU-L: PASS (tight on fairness in overload but still under 1500ms with current knobs)

============================================================
TAB: Open questions / TODO
============================================================
- Tune short_weight per tier/route? Dedicated customers may accept +2–3% short p95 for better long p95.
- Classification sensitivity: for TR-02, classifier sometimes labels “medium” requests as short; need audit of borderline prompt sizes (see ENG-4831).
- Consider adding a “medium” bucket later? (out of scope for prototype; but L40S results suggest two buckets may be too coarse on smaller SKUs)
- Validate multi-GPU (tensor parallel) effects: queueing interacts with microbatch formation; not covered here.
